metadata.title: Bufala
metadata.description: Got a strange message? Bufala helps you tell whether it's a scam.

what.title: What Bufala is
what.body: Bufala helps you tell whether a message is a scam. We built it above all for older people, whom scammers target most often.

free.title: Free, with no advertising
free.body: Bufala is free, shows no advertising and doesn't sell your data. We plan to fund it through grants and donations.

never.title: Bufala will never ask you for anything
never.body: Bufala will never ask you for money, codes, passwords or personal details, and it will never contact you by phone, SMS or email. If someone does so in Bufala's name, it's a scam.

independent.title: Independent
independent.body: Bufala is not connected to any bank, company or public office, and doesn't speak for them.

how.title: How it works
how.body: We compare the message's links and numbers with our own list of official sites and numbers, and have an artificial-intelligence system read the message after hiding its most sensitive details. We don't store the message.

contact.title: Contact
contact.body: Write to us at [TO COMPLETE: email address].

notFound.title: Page not found
notFound.body: This page doesn't exist. Maybe the address is mistyped, or the link is old.

errorPage.title: Something went wrong
errorPage.body: It's not your fault. Please try again in a moment.

home.title: Bufala
home.tagline: Got a strange message? Let's check it together.

check.label: Paste the message you received here
check.screenshotButton: Upload a screenshot of the message
check.screenshotPreview: Preview of the screenshot to check

errors.empty: First paste the message you want to check, or upload a screenshot.
errors.too_long: The message is too long. Paste just the main part.
errors.unavailable: We couldn't check the message. Please try again in a few minutes.
errors.invalid_image: This file doesn't look like a screenshot. Upload a JPG or PNG image, or paste the text instead.
errors.unreadable_image: We can't read the text in this image. Try a sharper screenshot, or paste the text instead.
errors.rate_limited: You've made a lot of checks in a short time. To protect the service, please try again in a few minutes.

scam.title: Very likely a scam
scam.body: Don't open any links, don't call any numbers and don't reply to this message.

suspicious.title: Suspicious: don't do what it asks
suspicious.body: Something isn't right. Before you do anything, check another way.

no_signs.title: No warning signs found
no_signs.body: We didn't find any signs of a scam, but that doesn't mean the message is safe.

result.genericReason: The message looks like the most common scams.
result.lookalikeOf: The link goes to a site that imitates {name}, but it isn't its official site.
result.safeStepOfficial: Call {name} on its official {count, plural, one {number} other {numbers}} {phones}, or open its app or website yourself. Don't use any links or numbers from the message.

phoneLabel.accounts_cards: for accounts, cards and the app
phoneLabel.parcels_landline: for parcels and letters, free from a landline
phoneLabel.free_others: free from landlines or other networks

result.genuinePayment: {name} really can ask for a payment by message. Before paying, check on its official website yourself, typing the address by hand, or call its official number.

signs.lookalike_link: The link goes to a site that imitates a well-known company's, but it isn't its official site.
signs.premium_number: It contains a premium-rate number: calling it can cost a lot.
signs.shortened_link: It contains a shortened link, which hides the site it really goes to.
signs.asks_for_code: It asks for a code, a PIN or a password. Banks and public offices never ask for these by message.
signs.asks_for_payment: It asks you to pay or transfer money.
signs.asks_for_personal_data: It asks for your personal, card or account details.
signs.install_app: It asks you to install an app, which could be used to control your phone.
signs.new_number_family: It says it's a relative or friend writing from a new number.
signs.threat: It threatens consequences, like a blocked account or a fine, to scare you.
signs.urgency: It rushes you. Someone genuinely writing to you gives you time to check.
signs.link_to_act: It asks you to open a link to sort out a problem.
signs.call_this_number: It asks you to call a number written in the message.
signs.shows_code: It contains a security code. If you didn't start this yourself, someone may be trying to use your account: don't give the code to anyone.
signs.prize_or_refund: It promises a prize, a refund or a bonus you weren't expecting.
signs.parcel_problem: It talks about a parcel that's held up or a delivery you have to pay for.
signs.secrecy: It asks you not to tell anyone.

safeStep.bank: Call your bank on the number on the back of your card, or open the bank's app yourself. Don't use any links or numbers from the message.
safeStep.poste: Open the Poste Italiane app yourself or go to a post office. Don't use any links or numbers from the message.
safeStep.phone_operator: Open your phone company's app yourself, or call the number on its official website.
safeStep.utility: Check your bills in your supplier's customer area, opening it yourself, or call the number printed on your bill.
safeStep.public_body: Check the office's official website, typing the address yourself, or call the number listed there.
safeStep.courier: Check the delivery on the website of the shop you bought from, or on the courier's website, typing the address yourself.
safeStep.family: Call the person on the number you've always used, not the new one. Or ask them something only they would know.
safeStep.other: Don't use any links or numbers from the message. If you know who it claims to be from, contact them yourself using details you already have.

result.reminder: Remember: if they ask for money or codes, contact the company or the person yourself, on a number you already know.
